payload.claim: [host-filed criterion probe] tests/test_intake.py::test_every_reader_of_the_retired_directory_name_imports_it_from_intake stayed green with the spec's wrong version '`worktree.py` builds `SPEC_ID_DIRS` without reading the name.' applied to saffron/cell/worktree.py as an edit. The claim was 'Every Python file under `saffron/` and `tests/` that reads `RETIRED_DIRNAME` reads it through `saffron.intake`, either as `from saffron.intake import RETIRED_DIRNAME` or as an attribute of the `intake` module. The witness collects each import naming the name, each attribute read of it and each assignment to it. It proves that walk on a sample first. The sample imports the name from `saffron.intake` and from `saffron.scheduler`. It reads it as an attribute of `intake`, of `saffron.intake` and of `scheduler`, and assigns it once. The witness asserts the exact routes and the one assignment. It then walks every file. Exactly one file assigns it, and that file is `saffron/intake.py`. No import of the name comes from another module, and no attribute read of it goes through another module. Each of `saffron/scheduler.py`, `saffron/draft.py`, `saffron/follow_up.py`, `saffron/cli.py`, `saffron/cell/worktree.py` and `tests/test_cli.py` reads it through `saffron.intake`.'. Under the edit the whole `tests` gate failed tests/test_intake.py::test_only_intake_spells_the_retired_directory_in_saffron_source, tests/test_saffron_gates.py::test_the_fast_gates_name_their_tool_and_pass_on_a_clean_tree[lint], and the criterion's witness did not fail.
